features.name: Darkvision
features.description: You gain darkvision 60 feet, or extend existing darkvision by 30 feet. From 13th level, you can see through magical darkness too.

features.name: Marked for Death
features.description: If a melee weapon attack against a creature you have marked deals more damage than its remaining hit points, it drops to 0 hit points.

features.name: Undead Empathy
features.description: An Undead that targets you with an attack must first make a Wisdom save (DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Constitution modifier); on a failure the attack misses, and if its Intelligence is 4 or less it is friendly to you and your allies for 1 minute.

features.name: Evasion
features.description: When an effect lets you make a Dexterity save for half damage, you take none on a success and half on a failure.

features.name: Gravelord
features.description: Once per long rest, as an action, take on undeath for 1 minute: immunity to poison damage and the poisoned condition; Undying usable three times per long rest instead of once; and once per turn, when your melee weapon attack damages a hostile creature, add 4d6 necrotic damage and gain that much temporary hit points until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: You learn two druid cantrips (a third at 10th level) and know three 1st-level druid spells, two of which must be evocation or transmutation. Later spells must be evocation or transmutation except those gained at 8th, 14th, and 20th level, which can be any school; you can swap one known spell per warden level under the same rule. Slots return on a long rest; Wisdom is your spellcasting ability (save DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier; attack modifier proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier). Spells known: 3 at 3rd, 4 at 4th-6th, 5 at 7th, 6 at 8th-9th, 7 at 10th, 8 at 11th-12th, 9 at 13th, 10 at 14th-15th, 11 at 16th-18th, 12 at 19th, 13 at 20th. Slots (1st/2nd/3rd/4th): 2 at 3rd; 3 at 4th-6th; 4/2 at 7th-9th; 4/3 at 10th-12th; 4/3/2 at 13th-15th; 4/3/3 at 16th-18th; 4/3/3/1 at 19th-20th.

features.name: Soulblood
features.description: When a creature within 5 feet damages you, you can mark it as a reaction.

features.name: Whispers of Beyond
features.description: Spend 1 minute in contemplation when making an Intelligence or Wisdom check to gain advantage, provided your ancestors could plausibly know the answer.

features.name: Spell Resistance
features.description: You have advantage on saving throws against spells.

features.name: Ethereal Watcher
features.description: Once per long rest, as an action, become spirit-like for 1 minute: as a bonus action you can turn ethereal as per etherealness; you can use your bonus action to return when you use Warden's Mark or Warden's Grasp, or when you cast a spell on your turn; on returning, creatures you choose within 10 feet take 4d6 force damage; and you can cast your known 1st- and 2nd-level druid spells without spending slots.

features.name: Roots of Rock
features.description: Using Warden's Grasp gives you +2 AC until the start of your next turn. Also, until you move, hostile effects can't shove or push you unless you allow it, you have advantage on Strength saves against being knocked prone, you can't slip or fall from ledges, and you are immune to fly, levitate, and telekinesis.

features.name: Earthshatter
features.description: You can use Warden's Grasp as an action instead; each affected creature must pass a Strength save (DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength modifier) or fall prone. Uses equal your Strength modifier (minimum 1), restored on a long rest.

features.name: Mettle
features.description: When an effect lets you make a Constitution save for half damage, you take none on a success and half on a failure.

features.name: Immortal Mountain
features.description: Once per long rest, as an action, encase yourself in stone for 1 minute: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage you take is reduced by 5, Roots of Rock applies the whole time, and you can leave a 5-foot-wide trail of difficult terrain as you move.

features.name: Thunderblast
features.description: When you hit a creature you have marked with a melee weapon attack, creatures you choose within 5 feet of it take 1d8 lightning damage.

features.name: Flash from Above
features.description: While under open sky, you can use an action to produce a harmless but dramatic lightning bolt or thunderclap, even without clouds.

features.name: Static Burst
features.description: When you use Warden's Grasp as a bonus action, affected creatures can't take reactions until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Evasion
features.description: When an effect lets you make a Dexterity save for half damage, you take none on a success and half on a failure.

features.name: Stormlord
features.description: You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed. Once per long rest, as an action, call lightning onto yourself for 1 minute: your flying speed doubles, and you can cast call lightning as a bonus action without a slot (DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Constitution modifier), calling later bolts as a bonus action.

features.name: Green Mark
features.description: While a creature you have marked is within 30 feet of you, the ground it moves across is difficult terrain.

features.name: Verdant Skin
features.description: You gain Stealth proficiency if you lack it. As an action, wrap yourself in vines and leaves; until you move, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in vegetation.

features.name: Mettle
features.description: When an effect lets you make a Constitution save for half damage, you take none on a success and half on a failure.

features.name: Form of the Oak Sentinel
features.description: Once per long rest, as an action, transform for 1 minute: your AC becomes 20 if lower, your melee attacks have 10-foot reach, and you can use Warden's Grasp as an action to make a separate attack against each affected creature.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: You gain Intelligence-based slot spellcasting from the wizard spell list; slots return on a long rest. You start knowing three 1st-level wizard spells, two of which must be conjuration or evocation, and every later spell must be conjuration or evocation except the ones gained at 8th, 14th, and 20th level. Each warmage level you may swap one known wizard spell for another of a level you have slots for (subject to the same school limit). By warmage level (spells known, slots 1st/2nd/3rd/4th): 3: 3 known, slots 2; 4: 4 known, slots 3; 5: 4 known, slots 3; 6: 4 known, slots 3; 7: 5 known, slots 4/2; 8: 6 known, slots 4/2; 9: 6 known, slots 4/2; 10: 7 known, slots 4/3; 11: 8 known, slots 4/3; 12: 8 known, slots 4/3; 13: 9 known, slots 4/3/2; 14: 10 known, slots 4/3/2; 15: 10 known, slots 4/3/2; 16: 11 known, slots 4/3/3; 17: 11 known, slots 4/3/3; 18: 11 known, slots 4/3/3; 19: 12 known, slots 4/3/3/1; 20: 13 known, slots 4/3/3/1. Warmage Edge applies to your leveled warmage spells as if they were cantrips, except magic missile.

features.name: Arcane Study
features.description: Gain proficiency in two of Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, or Religion.

features.name: Mystical Companion
features.description: You learn find familiar as a ritual, free of your spells known, and can pick an imp, pseudodragon, quasit, or sprite form in addition to the usual forms.

features.name: Siege Casting
features.description: Your warmage spells deal double damage to objects and structures. Spells of yours that use a spell attack can reach up to twice their normal range, with disadvantage on the attack beyond normal range.

features.name: Spell Sculpting
features.description: When your warmage spell affects creatures you can see, choose up to your Intelligence modifier of them: they automatically succeed on their saves and take no damage where a success would normally halve it.

features.name: Arcane Dominance
features.description: As a bonus action, spend spell slots totaling 6 or more levels to recover one expended use of Arcane Surge.

features.name: Bluff
features.description: Gain proficiency in Deception and the playing card set (if you lack them), and you can use Intelligence instead of Charisma for Charisma (Deception) checks.

features.name: Deck of Fate
features.description: When you roll initiative, shuffle a standard 52-card deck and draw five. When you target a hostile creature with a damaging warmage spell, you can spend your bonus action to play cards from your hand; if they form an exact hand from the table, one chosen target takes extra damage or you gain an effect (aces count as 1). Hands: Straight (any five in sequence) +12 damage; Flush (five of one suit) +10 damage; Three of a Kind +6 damage; Pair +2 damage; two Hearts, temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier; two Spades, +10 feet speed until the start of your next turn; two Diamonds, +1 AC until the start of your next turn; two Clubs, +1 to saving throws until the start of your next turn. Played cards go to the bottom of the deck and you draw back up to five. Unmatched cards do nothing.

features.name: High Stakes
features.description: On your turn, with no action, put any number of cards from your hand on the bottom of the deck, losing 2 hit points per card, then draw back up to five.

features.name: Dealer's Choice
features.description: As a bonus action, gain one effect that the GM picks: resistance to all damage until the end of your next turn; teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet; or vanish into a safe demiplane until the start of your next turn, returning to the spot you left. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Card Reading
features.description: Once per turn when you draw for Deck of Fate, name a suit and look at the top card; if you named it correctly, you can also take the Dash, Disengage, or Use an Object action as part of that bonus action.

features.name: Ace in the Hole
features.description: Whenever you draw cards, draw twice as many, put half on the bottom of the deck, and keep the rest.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: Gain proficiency in Sleight of Hand and the dice set if you lack them.

features.name: Dice of Fate
features.description: You have four Dice of Fate (d6s). Spend one to add it to an ability check, attack roll, saving throw, or damage roll; spent dice pass to the GM, who can add one to an NPC or monster roll, after which it returns to you. A long rest restores all your dice whether or not the GM used them. At 7th level you gain two more dice and can add two Dice of Fate to damage rolls of your warmage spells.

features.name: Chaos Roll
features.description: As an action, spend two Dice of Fate and roll them (2d6): 2, you cast fireball centered on yourself; 3, your AC drops by 2 until the start of your next turn; 4, you fall prone; 5, every other creature within 60 feet can only babble for 1 minute and can't supply verbal components; 6, a 5-foot-radius sphere of butterflies, insects, or doves heavily obscures a point within 60 feet until the start of your next turn; 7, gain 7 temporary hit points and keep both dice instead of giving them to the GM; 8, you turn invisible (as invisibility) until the end of your next turn; 9, a random object within 60 feet explodes, dealing 3d6 fire damage to one creature the GM chooses and none to you or allies; 10, teleport up to 60 feet to a space you can see, and each creature within 5 feet of the destination makes a Dexterity save or takes 2d6 force damage; 11, a creature you can see within 60 feet takes 4d6 necrotic damage and you heal that much; 12, you cast lightning bolt and may add Dice of Fate to its damage.

features.name: Loaded Dice
features.description: Once per turn when you roll a d6, you can turn it over so the opposite face (7 minus the result) counts instead.

features.name: Twisted Fate
features.description: When you make an attack roll or ability check with disadvantage on your turn, you can use a bonus action to spend and roll a Die of Fate: on a 5 you ignore the disadvantage, and on a 6 you have advantage instead.

features.name: Roll the Bones
features.description: When a creature you can see damages you, you can use your reaction and spend two Dice of Fate to make a Chaos Roll.

features.name: Steal Luck
features.description: When you roll initiative, roll a d6 and reclaim that many Dice of Fate from the GM.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: Gain proficiency with medium armor, battleaxes, lances, longswords, tridents, and warhammers.

features.name: Battle Tactics
features.description: You fuel stratagems with battle dice: 2d8 at 3rd level, 3d8 at 7th, 3d10 at 13th, and 4d10 at 19th. All spent dice return on a short or long rest or when you roll initiative. You can use one stratagem per turn, and stratagem saves use your spell save DC. Stratagems: Blitz (bonus action after hitting with an attack; an ally who can see or hear you can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks from your target); Check (bonus action after a hit; the target makes a Charisma save, auto-success if immune to charm, or must use its reaction to move up to half its speed directly away from you); Flash of Brilliance (add the die to an Intelligence or Wisdom check, even after rolling but before the result is known); Gambit (after a hit, the next creature other than you to attack the target adds the die to its attack roll); Mystic Counsel (bonus action, a creature within 30 feet that can hear you can add the die to one save against a spell in the next minute); Stalemate (bonus action after a hit; until the end of its next turn the target can't move willingly unless it first Disengages).

features.name: Lead from the Front
features.description: You and allies within 120 feet who can see you ignore nonmagical difficult terrain.

features.name: Tactical Master
features.description: Friendly creatures within 10 feet of you add your Intelligence modifier to saves against damaging spells and magical effects.

features.name: Stratagem: Checkmate
features.description: New stratagem: after hitting with a weapon or spell attack, use a bonus action and a battle die so an ally who can see or hear you and is within reach of the target can immediately use its reaction to make one weapon attack or cast an attack-roll cantrip, adding the die to that attack's damage.

features.name: Grandmaster
features.description: When you roll initiative, up to your Intelligence modifier of allies who can see or hear you each get a free battle die (no expenditure). Once within 10 minutes, each can add it to an ability check, attack roll, damage roll, or save, deciding after the roll but before the outcome is declared. A creature can hold only one such die at a time.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: Gain proficiency with medium armor and martial weapons.

features.name: Force Breastplate
features.description: While in light or medium armor or under mage armor, you use your Intelligence modifier in place of Dexterity for your AC.

features.name: Mystical Weapon
features.description: You learn force weapon as a bonus cantrip. Whenever you would draw a weapon on your turn, you can instead conjure any simple or martial weapon of force into an empty hand; it counts as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity and disappears if it leaves your hand.

features.name: Flurry of Blades
features.description: When you cast a cantrip that makes multiple spell attacks (such as force weapon or magic daggers), you can use your bonus action to make one more attack with it.

features.name: Knight's Ward
features.description: As a bonus action, gain temporary hit points equal to twice your warmage level for 1 minute. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Tactical Maneuver
features.description: You can spend all of your movement to teleport up to half your speed to an unoccupied space you can see.

features.name: Field of Blades
features.description: As an action, make separate melee spell attacks against up to five creatures you can see within 30 feet; each hit deals 2d10 + your Intelligence modifier force damage.

features.name: Intercept Technique
features.description: With no armor and no shield, your AC is 10 + Dexterity modifier + Intelligence modifier; under mage armor it is 13 + your choice of Dexterity or Intelligence modifier. Using a shield removes this benefit.

features.name: Hand-to-Hand Arcana
features.description: Your unarmed strikes can use Intelligence for attack and damage rolls, can deal 1d6 in place of their normal damage, and count as melee weapons for warmage spells.

features.name: Shock Trooper
features.description: When you make a melee attack on your turn against a creature you can see, you can first lunge up to 15 feet toward it without provoking opportunity attacks, even through the air (you fall after the attack if not on solid ground).

features.name: Mystical Physicality
features.description: You can use your Intelligence modifier for Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution checks, and difficult terrain costs you no extra movement.

features.name: Deflect Energy
features.description: When a ranged spell attack or ranged weapon attack dealing cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, or radiant damage hits you, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by 1d10 + your Intelligence modifier + half your warmage level (rounded down).

features.name: Improved Shock Trooper
features.description: Your Shock Trooper lunge reaches 30 feet and becomes a teleport that passes through creatures and objects, though you can't end in an occupied space.

features.name: Flurry of Spells
features.description: As an action, spend an Arcane Surge use to cast three different cantrips that each take 1 action or 1 bonus action; Arcane Surge can't apply to them. Once per long rest.

features.name: Promotion
features.description: Learn one extra warmage trick that doesn't count against tricks known. Whenever you learn a trick, you can pick ones requiring the House of Bishops, Kings, Knights, or Rooks, provided you meet their other prerequisites.

features.name: Adaptive Arcanist
features.description: After each short or long rest, pick a warmage cantrip; you know it (not counted against cantrips known) until you pick another with this feature.

features.name: Pawn Storm
features.description: A creature you target with a cantrip can't make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of the turn, whether or not the cantrip damaged it.

features.name: Additional Arcane Fighting Style
features.description: Choose a second option from Arcane Fighting Style.

features.name: Opening Move
features.description: Add your Intelligence modifier to initiative, and when you roll initiative while not surprised you can move up to your speed.

features.name: Fundamental Mastery
features.description: Once per turn when rolling damage for a warmage cantrip, treat one damage die as its maximum result.

features.name: Rook Strike
features.description: As a bonus action, gain advantage on your next spell attack roll this turn, or give a creature disadvantage on its save against a warmage spell you cast before your turn ends. Recharges on a short or long rest, or when a cantrip of yours drops a creature to 0 hit points.

features.name: Rasp
features.description: You can cast knock at will without a spell slot; cast this way it takes 1 minute and makes no sound.

features.name: Arcane Acrobat
features.description: Add your Intelligence modifier to every Dexterity check, and when you fall while not incapacitated you can reduce the fall by up to 60 feet for damage purposes.

features.name: Fleeting Decoy
features.description: When a creature you can see damages you, you can use your reaction so attacks against you have disadvantage until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Elusive Step
features.description: Once you have moved more than 15 feet on your turn, your further movement that turn doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

features.name: Flash of Feathers
features.description: Cast invisibility on yourself only, with no slot or components. While invisible this way your speed doubles, and you can make one attack or cast one warmage cantrip without ending the invisibility. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Black Magic Spells
features.description: Learned craft spells (count as witch spells, not against spells known), by spell level: 1st exhume, inflict wounds; 2nd gentle repose, magic weapon; 3rd animate dead, vampiric touch; 4th blight, death ward; 5th cloudkill, contagion.

features.name: Hex: Decay
features.description: Action, one creature you can see within 60 feet makes a Constitution save; on a failure at the start of its next turn it suffers 1d4 necrotic damage and its hit point maximum drops by that amount while the hex lasts, killing it if the maximum reaches 0. Ends at the end of your next turn.

features.name: Undeath Command
features.description: The bonus action you use to command your familiar can also command any Undead you control through animate dead or similar magic.

features.name: Life Tether
features.description: When a creature you can see damages you, you can use your reaction to split the damage with the sole target of your hex: you take half (rounded down) and it takes the rest. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Black Sacrifice
features.description: As an action with your familiar within 10 feet, you sacrifice its bond: creatures you choose within 20 feet of it make a Dexterity save against your spell save DC, taking 8d10 necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success, and their hit point maximum drops by the necrotic damage taken (dying at 0). The familiar can't be summoned again before your next long rest.

features.name: Blood Magic Spells
features.description: Learned craft spells (count as witch spells, not against spells known), by spell level: 1st hellish rebuke, hollowing curse; 2nd acid arrow, hold person; 3rd ruby-eye curse, vampiric touch; 4th blight, dominate beast; 5th cloudkill, dominate person.

features.name: Hex: Blood Curse
features.description: Action, one creature you can see within 60 feet makes a Constitution save; on a failure, until the end of your next turn, the moment it is both injured and under twice your witch level in hit points, it falls to 0 hit points.

features.name: Novice Hemomancy
features.description: A drop of your blood can replace material components that have no listed cost.

features.name: Arcane Bloodletting
features.description: When casting a spell with a casting time of 1 action, lose 5 hit points to cast it as a bonus action instead. Uses equal your Charisma modifier (minimum 1), restored on a long rest.

features.name: Deathseeker
features.description: You sense the location of any creature within 60 feet that is missing hit points, even when heavily obscured and through most barriers (stopped by a foot of stone, an inch of ordinary metal, a thin lead sheet, or 3 feet of wood or earth). You have advantage on checks to track a creature you or your familiar damaged in the last 24 hours.

features.name: Hemomantic Recovery
features.description: Once per day after a short rest, spend Hit Dice to regain spell slots of 5th level or lower: 2 Hit Dice for 1st, 3 for 2nd, 5 for 3rd, 6 for 4th, 7 for 5th.

features.name: Sanguine
features.description: Once per round, when your spell hurts a hostile creature that is your hex's only target, you can lose hit points to add 2d8 necrotic damage per 5 hit points lost, up to 6d8.

features.name: Green Magic Spells
features.description: Learned craft spells (count as witch spells, not against spells known), by spell level: 1st entangle, goodberry; 2nd barkskin, locate animals or plants; 3rd conjure animals, plant growth; 4th conjure woodland beings, stoneskin; 5th awaken, tree stride.

features.name: Hex: Elder Tongue
features.description: As a bonus action, until the end of your next turn you can communicate in a limited way with Beasts and Plants (they can relay simple recent observations) and have advantage on Charisma checks to influence them.

features.name: Primal Ally
features.description: Your familiar adds three times your witch level to its hit point maximum instead of twice.

features.name: Twin Familiar
features.description: When summoned, your familiar can be split into two identical bodies sharing one hit point pool, acting on consecutive turns. Command one to attack with your bonus action and the other with your action; effects that target or dismiss the familiar affect both.

features.name: Vital Nourishment
features.description: When you finish a long rest, plants within 120 feet grow as if a month of ideal conditions passed, and food-bearing plants yield enough to feed six creatures for a day. Up to six creatures you can see gain temporary hit points of half your witch level + Charisma modifier, and you can end one disease or one blinded, deafened, paralyzed, or poisoned condition on each.

features.name: Sacrificial Familiar
features.description: When a melee attack targets you with your familiar within 5 feet, you can use your reaction to have the attack target the familiar instead. Uses equal your Charisma modifier (minimum 1), restored on a long rest.

features.name: Purple Magic Spells
features.description: Learned craft spells (count as witch spells, not against spells known), by spell level: 1st charm person, silent image; 2nd enthrall, invisibility; 3rd hypnotic pattern, major image; 4th confusion, private sanctum; 5th modify memory, seeming.

features.name: Hex: Hallucination
features.description: Action, one creature you can see within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save (auto-success if immune to charm); on a failure it takes -1 to attack rolls and ability checks, worsening by 1 at the start of each of its turns to a maximum of -5. Lasts until the end of your next turn.

features.name: False Authority
features.description: As an action, everyone who sees you perceives you as an authority figure relevant to them for 1 hour (or until you end it); it doesn't survive physical inspection, and a creature can use its action and an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC to see through it. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Deceitful Transposition
features.description: As a bonus action, make two creatures within 60 feet appear to have swapped places, relocating their sounds, smells, and other cues; they don't perceive the illusion. An observer can use its action and an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC to see the truth. Lasts 1 minute, ending early if either takes damage or a physical interaction exposes it. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Waking Nightmare
features.description: When a creature fails its save against your Hallucination hex, you can make it treat every creature as an enemy until the hex ends: it picks targets for attacks, spells, and effects at random among creatures in range it can see, and must use its reaction on any opportunity attack offered. Ends after 1 minute. Once per long rest.

features.name: Red Magic Spells
features.description: Learned craft spells (count as witch spells, not against spells known), by spell level: 1st burning hands, magic missile; 2nd acid arrow, scorching ray; 3rd fireball, protection from energy; 4th ice storm, wall of fire; 5th cone of cold, telekinesis.

features.name: Hex: Imperil
features.description: Action, choose a damage type and one creature you can see within 60 feet, which makes a Constitution save; on a failure its resistance to that type is suppressed through the end of your next turn, and immunity to it is downgraded to resistance.

features.name: Convolute Energy
features.description: Casting a spell that deals acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage can grant you resistance to that damage type through the end of your next turn.

features.name: Invulnerability
features.description: When an attacker you can see hits you, use your reaction to reduce the damage by 50. Once per long rest.

features.name: Elemental Annihilation
features.description: When you cast a witch spell dealing acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can spend an additional slot of equal or higher level to deal maximum damage. Once per long rest.

features.name: Steel Magic Spells
features.description: Learned craft spells (count as witch spells, not against spells known), by spell level: 1st heroism, shield; 2nd heat metal, magic weapon; 3rd blink, haste; 4th death ward, freedom of movement; 5th flame strike, telekinesis.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: Gain proficiency with martial melee weapons that lack the heavy and special properties.

features.name: Hex: Malevolence
features.description: As a bonus action, wrap yourself in evil smog until the end of your next turn; damage can't break your concentration on it. While active: AC 12 + Dexterity modifier + Charisma modifier without a shield (usable if better than your armor); use Charisma for attack and damage with melee weapons lacking heavy and special; and a visible creature within 5 feet that damages you can be answered with a melee weapon attack as your reaction.

features.name: Cackling Killer
features.description: On a turn you use Cackle, you attack twice instead of once when you take the Attack action.

features.name: Soulsword Familiar
features.description: As a bonus action, dismiss your familiar into your weapon, wreathing it in green flame; it deals an extra 1d8 fire damage on a hit until you resummon the familiar, which you can't do until a short or long rest.

features.name: Shrieking Strike
features.description: Once per turn when you hit with a melee weapon attack, the target makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC or is frightened of you for up to 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns. Uses equal your Charisma modifier (minimum 1), restored on a long rest.

features.name: Tea Magic Spells
features.description: Learned craft spells (count as witch spells, not against spells known), by spell level: 1st hideous laughter, sanctuary; 2nd augury, calm emotions; 3rd clairvoyance, sending; 4th divination, private sanctum; 5th legend lore, scrying.

features.name: Hex: Tasseography
features.description: Action, pick an ally you can see within 60 feet and roll a d20, noting the result. Until the end of your next turn you can substitute that number for one attack roll, saving throw, or ability check the ally makes, chosen before it rolls; the hex then ends.

features.name: Tea Ceremony
features.description: During a short or long rest you conjure tea for yourself and allies; each creature that drinks it removes one extra level of exhaustion during that rest.

features.name: Shapes and Omens
features.description: After a long rest, the GM describes a shape in your tea leaves that hints at upcoming events.

features.name: Herbal Remedy
features.description: Cast greater restoration without a slot or material components. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Invigorate
features.description: As a bonus action, you or an ally you can see within 5 feet gains one extra action on its next turn. Once per long rest.

features.name: Technicolor Magic Spells
features.description: Learned craft spells (count as witch spells, not against spells known), by spell level: 1st color spray, speak with animals; 2nd animal messenger, warding bond; 3rd fly, sending; 4th freedom of movement, locate creature; 5th telepathic bond, teleportation circle.

features.name: Hex: Musical Interlude
features.description: Action, each willing creature within 30 feet that you can see and that can see you gains temporary hit points of half your witch level + Charisma modifier, lasting through the end of your next turn.

features.name: Animal Friends
features.description: Advantage on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks to befriend Beasts, using Charisma instead of Wisdom for Small or smaller ones. You can dismiss an adopted Beast pet into an extradimensional space as you would a familiar.

features.name: Friendship Bracelet
features.description: As an action, craft a cheap bracelet. You always know the location of a creature wearing one while on the same plane and can aim spells and effects at it without needing sight of it.

features.name: Positivity
features.description: When an attacker you can see hits you, your reaction adds to your AC one point per friendly creature within 5 feet of you, possibly causing a miss. Once per short or long rest.

features.name: Redemptive Arc

Once per long rest.

When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes 2d6 damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 16th level. After you use your breath weapon, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

background:urchin-baldur-s-gate.equipment: A small knife, a map of the city you grew up in, a pet mouse, a token to remember your parents by, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 gp

rule:grappling.description:
When you want to grab a creature or wrestle with it, you can use the Attack action to make a special melee attack, a grapple. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them.

The target of your grapple must be no more than one size larger than you and must be within your reach. Using at least one free hand, you try to seize the target by making a grapple check instead of an attack roll: a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (the target chooses the ability to use). If you succeed, you subject the target to the grappled condition. The condition specifies the things that end it, and you can release the target whenever you like (no action required).

rule:escaping-a-grapple.description: A grappled creature can use its action to escape. To do so, it must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by your Strength (Athletics) check.

rule:moving-a-grappled-creature.description: When you move, you can drag or carry the grappled creature with you, but your speed is halved, unless the creature is two or more sizes smaller than you.

rule:shoving-a-creature.description:
Using the Attack action, you can make a special melee attack to shove a creature, either to knock it prone or push it away from you. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them.

The target must be no more than one size larger than you and must be within your reach. Instead of making an attack roll, you make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (the target chooses the ability to use). If you win the contest, you either knock the target prone or push it 5 feet away from you.

rule:opportunity-attacks.description:
You can make an opportunity attack when a hostile creature that you can see moves out of your reach. To make the opportunity attack, you use your reaction to make one melee attack against the provoking creature. The attack occurs right before the creature leaves your reach.

You can avoid provoking an opportunity attack by taking the Disengage action. You also don't provoke an opportunity attack when you teleport or when someone or something moves you without using your movement, action, or reaction. For example, you don't provoke an opportunity attack if an explosion hurls you out of a foe's reach or if gravity causes you to fall past an enemy.

rule:unarmed-strike.description: Instead of using a weapon to make a melee weapon attack, you can use an unarmed strike: a punch, kick, head-butt, or similar forceful blow (none of which count as weapons). On a hit, an unarmed strike deals bludgeoning damage equal to 1 + your Strength modifier. You are proficient with your unarmed strikes.

rule:two-weapon-fighting.description:
When you take the Attack action and attack with a light melee weapon that you're holding in one hand, you can use a bonus action to attack with a different light melee weapon that you're holding in the other hand. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative.

If either weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon, instead of making a melee attack with it.

rule:ranged-attacks-in-close-combat.description: Aiming a ranged attack is more difficult when a foe is next to you. When you make a ranged attack with a weapon, a spell, or some other means, you have disadvantage on the attack roll if you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature who can see you and who isn't incapacitated.

rule:ranged-attack-range.description:
You can make ranged attacks only against targets within a specified range.

If a ranged attack, such as one made with a spell, has a single range, you can't attack a target beyond this range.

Some ranged attacks, such as those made with a longbow or a shortbow, have two ranges. The smaller number is the normal range, and the larger number is the long range. Your attack roll has disadvantage when your target is beyond normal range, and you can't attack a target beyond the long range.

rule:cover.description:
Walls, trees, creatures, and other obstacles can provide cover during combat, making a target more difficult to harm. A target can benefit from cover only when an attack or other effect originates on the opposite side of the cover.

There are three degrees of cover. If a target is behind multiple sources of cover, only the most protective degree of cover applies; the degrees aren't added together. For example, if a target is behind a creature that gives half cover and a tree trunk that gives three-quarters cover, the target has three-quarters cover.

A target with half cover has a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. A target has half cover if an obstacle blocks at least half of its body. The obstacle might be a low wall, a large piece of furniture, a narrow tree trunk, or a creature, whether that creature is an enemy or a friend.

A target with three-quarters cover has a +5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. A target has three-quarters cover if about three-quarters of it is covered by an obstacle. The obstacle might be a portcullis, an arrow slit, or a thick tree trunk.

A target with total cover can't be targeted directly by an attack or a spell, although some spells can reach such a target by including it in an area of effect. A target has total cover if it is completely concealed by an obstacle.

rule:critical-hits.description:
When you score a critical hit, you get to roll extra dice for the attack's damage against the target. Roll all of the attack's damage dice twice and add them together. Then add any relevant modifiers as normal. To speed up play, you can roll all the damage dice at once.

For example, if you score a critical hit with a dagger, roll 2d4 for the damage, rather than 1d4, and then add your relevant ability modifier. If the attack involves other damage dice, such as from the rogue's Sneak Attack feature, you roll those dice twice as well.

rule:damage-resistance-and-vulnerability.description:
If a creature or an object has resistance to a damage type, damage of that type is halved against it. If a creature or an object has vulnerability to a damage type, damage of that type is doubled against it.

Resistance and then vulnerability are applied after all other modifiers to damage. For example, a creature has resistance to bludgeoning damage and is hit by an attack that deals 25 bludgeoning damage. The creature is also within a magical aura that reduces all damage by 5. The 25 damage is first reduced by 5 and then halved, so the creature takes 10 damage.

Multiple instances of resistance or vulnerability that affect the same damage type count as only one instance. For example, if a creature has resistance to fire damage as well as resistance to all nonmagical damage, the damage of a nonmagical fire is reduced by half against the creature, not reduced by three-quarters.

rule:actions-in-combat.description:
When you take your action on your turn, you can take one of the actions presented here, an action you gained from your class or a special feature, or an action that you improvise.

The standard actions are: Attack, Cast a Spell, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide, Ready, Search, and Use an Object.

rule:dash.description: When you take the Dash action, you gain extra movement for the current turn. The increase equals your speed, after applying any modifiers.

rule:disengage.description: If you take the Disengage action, your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of the turn.

rule:dodge.description: When you take the Dodge action, you focus entirely on avoiding attacks. Until the start of your next turn, any attack roll made against you has disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you make Dexterity saving throws with advantage. You lose this benefit if you are incapacitated or if your speed drops to 0.

rule:help.description:
You can lend your aid to another creature in the completion of a task. When you take the Help action, the creature you aid gains advantage on the next ability check it makes to perform the task you are helping with, provided that it makes the check before the start of your next turn.

Alternatively, you can aid a friendly creature in attacking a creature within 5 feet of you. You feint, distract the target, or in some other way team up to make your ally's attack more effective. If your ally attacks the target before your next turn, the first attack roll is made with advantage.

rule:hide.description: When you take the Hide action, you make a Dexterity (Stealth) check in an attempt to hide, following the rules for hiding. If you succeed, you gain certain benefits, as described in the rules on unseen attackers and targets.

rule:ready.description:
Sometimes you want to get the jump on a foe or wait for a particular circumstance before you act. To do so, you can take the Ready action on your turn, which lets you act using your reaction before the start of your next turn.

First, you decide what perceivable circumstance will trigger your reaction. Then, you choose the action you will take in response to that trigger, or you choose to move up to your speed in response to it. When the trigger occurs, you can either take your reaction right after the trigger finishes or ignore the trigger.

When you ready a spell, you cast it as normal but hold its energy, which you release with your reaction when the trigger occurs. To be readied, a spell must have a casting time of 1 action, and holding onto the spell's magic requires concentration. If your concentration is broken, the spell dissipates without taking effect.

rule:search.description: When you take the Search action, you devote your attention to finding something. Depending on the nature of your search, the GM might have you make a Wisdom (Perception) check or an Intelligence (Investigation) check.

rule:use-an-object.description: You normally interact with an object while doing something else, such as when you draw a sword as part of an attack. When an object requires your action for its use, you take the Use an Object action. This action is also useful when you want to interact with more than one object on your turn.

rule:difficult-terrain.description:
Every foot of movement in difficult terrain costs 1 extra foot. This rule is true even if multiple things in a space count as difficult terrain.

Low furniture, rubble, undergrowth, steep stairs, snow, and shallow bogs are examples of difficult terrain. The space of another creature, whether hostile or not, also counts as difficult terrain.

rule:being-prone.description:
You can drop prone without using any of your speed. Standing up takes more effort; doing so costs an amount of movement equal to half your speed. For example, if your speed is 30 feet, you must spend 15 feet of movement to stand up. You can't stand up if you don't have enough movement left or if your speed is 0.

To move while prone, you must crawl or use magic such as teleportation. Every foot of movement while crawling costs 1 extra foot. Crawling 1 foot in difficult terrain, therefore, costs 3 feet of movement.

rule:moving-around-other-creatures.description:
You can move through a nonhostile creature's space. In contrast, you can move through a hostile creature's space only if the creature is at least two sizes larger or smaller than you. Remember that another creature's space is difficult terrain for you.

Whether a creature is a friend or an enemy, you can't willingly end your move in its space.

If you leave a hostile creature's reach during your move, you provoke an opportunity attack.

rule:squeezing-into-a-smaller-space.description: A creature can squeeze through a space that is large enough for a creature one size smaller than it. Thus, a Large creature can squeeze through a passage that's only 5 feet wide. While squeezing through a space, a creature must spend 1 extra foot for every foot it moves there, and it has disadvantage on attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws. Attack rolls against the creature have advantage while it's in the smaller space.

rule:vision-and-light.description:
A given area might be lightly or heavily obscured. In a lightly obscured area, such as dim light, patchy fog, or moderate foliage, creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

A heavily obscured area, such as darkness, opaque fog, or dense foliage, blocks vision entirely. A creature effectively suffers from the blinded condition when trying to see something in that area.

The presence or absence of light in an environment creates three categories of illumination: bright light, dim light, and darkness. Bright light lets most creatures see normally. Dim light, also called shadows, creates a lightly obscured area. Darkness creates a heavily obscured area.

Darkvision: Within a specified range, a creature with darkvision can see in darkness as if the darkness were dim light, so areas of darkness are only lightly obscured as far as that creature is concerned. However, the creature can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

Blindsight: A creature with blindsight can perceive its surroundings without relying on sight, within a specific radius.

Truesight: A creature with truesight can, out to a specific range, see in normal and magical darkness, see invisible creatures and objects, automatically detect visual illusions and succeed on saving throws against them, and perceives the original form of a shapechanger or a creature that is transformed by magic. Furthermore, the creature can see into the Ethereal Plane.

rule:falling.description: A fall from a great height is one of the most common hazards facing an adventurer. At the end of a fall, a creature takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it fell, to a maximum of 20d6. The creature lands prone, unless it avoids taking damage from the fall.

rule:suffocating.description:
A creature can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 + its Constitution modifier (minimum of 30 seconds).

When a creature runs out of breath or is choking, it can survive for a number of rounds equal to its Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 round). At the start of its next turn, it drops to 0 hit points and is dying, and it can't regain hit points or be stabilized until it can breathe again.

For example, a creature with a Constitution of 14 can hold its breath for 3 minutes. If it starts suffocating, it has 2 rounds to reach air before it drops to 0 hit points.

rule:short-rest.description:
A short rest is a period of downtime, at least 1 hour long, during which a character does nothing more strenuous than eating, drinking, reading, and tending to wounds.

A character can spend one or more Hit Dice at the end of a short rest, up to the character's maximum number of Hit Dice, which is equal to the character's level. For each Hit Die spent in this way, the player rolls the die and adds the character's Constitution modifier to it. The character regains hit points equal to the total. The player can decide to spend an additional Hit Die after each roll. A character regains some spent Hit Dice upon finishing a long rest.

rule:long-rest.description:
A long rest is a period of extended downtime, at least 8 hours long, during which a character sleeps or performs light activity: reading, talking, eating, or standing watch for no more than 2 hours. If the rest is interrupted by a period of strenuous activity, at least 1 hour of walking, fighting, casting spells, or similar adventuring activity, the characters must begin the rest again to gain any benefit from it.

At the end of a long rest, a character regains all lost hit points. The character also regains spent Hit Dice, up to a number of dice equal to half of the character's total number of them (minimum of one die). For example, if a character has eight Hit Dice, he or she can regain four spent Hit Dice upon finishing a long rest.

A character can't benefit from more than one long rest in a 24-hour period, and a character must have at least 1 hit point at the start of the rest to gain its benefits.

rule:dropping-to-0-hit-points.description:
When you drop to 0 hit points, you either die outright or fall unconscious, as explained in the following.

Instant Death: Massive damage can kill you instantly. When damage reduces you to 0 hit points and there is damage remaining, you die if the remaining damage equals or exceeds your hit point maximum. For example, a cleric with a maximum of 12 hit points currently has 6 hit points. If she takes 18 damage from an attack, she is reduced to 0 hit points, but 12 damage remains. Because the remaining damage equals her hit point maximum, the cleric dies.

Falling Unconscious: If damage reduces you to 0 hit points and fails to kill you, you fall unconscious. This unconsciousness ends if you regain any hit points.

rule:death-saving-throws.description:
Whenever you start your turn with 0 hit points, you must make a special saving throw, called a death saving throw, to determine whether you creep closer to death or hang onto life. Unlike other saving throws, this one isn't tied to any ability score.

Roll a d20. If the roll is 10 or higher, you succeed. Otherwise, you fail. A success or failure has no effect by itself. On your third success, you become stable. On your third failure, you die. The successes and failures don't need to be consecutive; keep track of both until you collect three of a kind. The number of both is reset to zero when you regain any hit points or become stable.

Rolling 1 or 20: When you make a death saving throw and roll a 1 on the d20, it counts as two failures. If you roll a 20 on the d20, you regain 1 hit point.

Damage at 0 Hit Points: If you take any damage while you have 0 hit points, you suffer a death saving throw failure. If the damage is from a critical hit, you suffer two failures instead. If the damage equals or exceeds your hit point maximum, you suffer instant death.

rule:stabilizing-a-creature.description:
The best way to save a creature with 0 hit points is to heal it. If healing is unavailable, the creature can at least be stabilized so that it isn't killed by a failed death saving throw.

You can use your action to administer first aid to an unconscious creature and attempt to stabilize it, which requires a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check.

A stable creature doesn't make death saving throws, even though it has 0 hit points, but it does remain unconscious. The creature stops being stable, and must start making death saving throws again, if it takes any damage. A stable creature that isn't healed regains 1 hit point after 1d4 hours.

rule:temporary-hit-points.description:
Temporary hit points aren't actual hit points; they are a buffer against damage, a pool of hit points that protect you from injury.

When you have temporary hit points and take damage, the temporary hit points are lost first, and any leftover damage carries over to your normal hit points. For example, if you have 5 temporary hit points and take 7 damage, you lose the temporary hit points and then take 2 damage.

Because temporary hit points are separate from your actual hit points, they can exceed your hit point maximum. A character can, therefore, be at full hit points and receive temporary hit points.

Healing can't restore temporary hit points, and they can't be added together. If you have temporary hit points and receive more of them, you decide whether to keep the ones you have or to gain the new ones. For example, if a spell grants you 12 temporary hit points when you already have 10, you can have 12 or 10, not 22.

Unless a feature that grants you temporary hit points has a duration, they last until they're depleted or you finish a long rest.

rule:spell-components.description:
A spell's components are the physical requirements you must meet in order to cast it. Each spell's description indicates whether it requires verbal (V), somatic (S), or material (M) components. If you can't provide one or more of a spell's components, you are unable to cast the spell.

Verbal (V): A character who is gagged or in an area of silence can't cast a spell with a verbal component.

Somatic (S): If a spell requires a somatic component, the caster must have free use of at least one hand to perform these gestures.

Material (M): A character can use a component pouch or a spellcasting focus in place of the components specified for a spell. But if a cost is indicated for a component, a character must have that specific component before he or she can cast the spell. If a spell states that a material component is consumed by the spell, the caster must provide this component for each casting. A spellcaster must have a hand free to access a spell's material components, or to hold a spellcasting focus, but it can be the same hand that he or she uses to perform somatic components.

rule:concentration.description:
Some spells require you to maintain concentration in order to keep their magic active. If you lose concentration, such a spell ends. You can end concentration at any time (no action required).

Normal activity, such as moving and attacking, doesn't interfere with concentration. The following factors can break concentration:

Casting another spell that requires concentration. You lose concentration on a spell if you cast another spell that requires concentration. You can't concentrate on two spells at once.

Taking damage. Whenever you take damage while you are concentrating on a spell, you must make a Constitution saving throw to maintain your concentration. The DC equals 10 or half the damage you take, whichever number is higher. If you take damage from multiple sources, you make a separate saving throw for each source of damage.

Being incapacitated or killed. You lose concentration on a spell if you are incapacitated or if you die.

rule:bonus-action-spells.description: A spell cast with a bonus action is especially swift. You must use a bonus action on your turn to cast the spell, provided that you haven't already taken a bonus action this turn. You can't cast another spell during the same turn, except for a cantrip with a casting time of 1 action.

rule:areas-of-effect.description:
A spell's description specifies its area of effect, which typically has one of five different shapes: cone, cube, cylinder, line, or sphere. Every area of effect has a point of origin, a location from which the spell's energy erupts. The rules for each shape specify how you position its point of origin.

A spell's effect expands in straight lines from the point of origin. If no unblocked straight line extends from the point of origin to a location within the area of effect, that location isn't included in the spell's area. To block one of these imaginary lines, an obstruction must provide total cover.

rule:a-clear-path-to-the-target.description:
To target something, you must have a clear path to it, so it can't be behind total cover.

If you place an area of effect at a point that you can't see and an obstruction, such as a wall, is between you and that point, the point of origin comes into being on the near side of that obstruction.

rule:advantage-and-disadvantage.description:
When you have advantage or disadvantage, you roll a second d20 when you make the roll. Use the higher of the two rolls if you have advantage, and use the lower roll if you have disadvantage.

If multiple situations affect a roll and each one grants advantage or imposes disadvantage on it, you don't roll more than one additional d20. If two favorable situations grant advantage, for example, you still roll only one additional d20.

If circumstances cause a roll to have both advantage and disadvantage, you are considered to have neither of them, and you roll one d20. This is true even if multiple circumstances impose disadvantage and only one grants advantage or vice versa.

When you have advantage or disadvantage and something in the game lets you reroll the d20, you can reroll only one of the dice. You choose which one.

rule:passive-checks.description:
A passive check is a special kind of ability check that doesn't involve any die rolls. Such a check can represent the average result for a task done repeatedly, such as searching for secret doors over and over again, or can be used when the GM wants to secretly determine whether the characters succeed at something without rolling dice, such as noticing a hidden monster.

Here's how to determine a character's total for a passive check: 10 + all modifiers that normally apply to the check. If the character has advantage on the check, add 5. For disadvantage, subtract 5. The game refers to a passive check total as a score.

For example, if a 1st-level character has a Wisdom of 15 and proficiency in Perception, he or she has a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 14.

rule:contests.description:
Sometimes one character's or monster's efforts are directly opposed to another's. In situations like these, the outcome is determined by a special form of ability check, called a contest.

Both participants in a contest make ability checks appropriate to their efforts. They apply all appropriate bonuses and penalties, but instead of comparing the total to a DC, they compare the totals of their two checks. The participant with the higher check total wins the contest.

If the contest results in a tie, the situation remains the same as it was before the contest. Thus, one contestant might win the contest by default.

rule:ammunition.description:
You can use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon).

At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield. If you use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a melee attack, you treat the weapon as an improvised weapon (see "Improvised Weapons" later in the section). A sling must be loaded to deal any damage when used in this way.

rule:finesse.description: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

rule:heavy.description: Small creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls with heavy weapons. A heavy weapon's size and bulk make it too large for a Small creature to use effectively.

rule:light.description: A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons.

rule:loading.description: Because of the time required to load this weapon, you can fire only one piece of ammunition from it when you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

rule:monk.description: Monks gain several benefits while unarmed or wielding only monk weapons while they aren't wearing armor or wielding shields.

rule:reach.description: This weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for opportunity attacks with it.

rule:special.description: A weapon with the special property has unusual rules governing its use, explained in the weapon's description (see "Special Weapons" later in this section).

rule:thrown.description: If a weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack. If the weapon is a melee weapon, you use the same ability modifier for that attack roll and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon. For example, if you throw a handaxe, you use your Strength, but if you throw a dagger, you can use either your Strength or your Dexterity, since the dagger has the finesse property.

rule:two-handed.description: This weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

rule:versatile.description: This weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property - the damage when the weapon is used with two hands to make a melee attack.

rule:mounted-combat.description:
A knight charging into battle on a warhorse, a wizard casting spells from the back of a griffon, or a cleric soaring through the sky on a pegasus all enjoy the benefits of speed and mobility that a mount can provide.

A willing creature that is at least one size larger than you and that has an appropriate anatomy can serve as a mount, using the following rules.

Mounting and Dismounting. Once during your move, you can mount a creature that is within 5 feet of you or dismount. Doing so costs an amount of movement equal to half your speed. For example, if your speed is 30 feet, you must spend 15 feet of movement to mount a horse. Therefore, you can't mount it if you don't have 15 feet of movement left or if your speed is 0.

If an effect moves your mount against its will while you're on it, you must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall off the mount, landing prone in a space within 5 feet of it. If you're knocked prone while mounted, you must make the same saving throw.

If your mount is knocked prone, you can use your reaction to dismount it as it falls and land on your feet. Otherwise, you are dismounted and fall prone in a space within 5 feet of it.

Controlling a Mount. While you're mounted, you have two options. You can either control the mount or allow it to act independently. Intelligent creatures, such as dragons, act independently.

You can control a mount only if it has been trained to accept a rider. Domesticated horses, donkeys, and similar creatures are assumed to have such training. The initiative of a controlled mount changes to match yours when you mount it. It moves as you direct it, and it has only three action options: Dash, Disengage, and Dodge. A controlled mount can move and act even on the turn that you mount it.

An independent mount retains its place in the initiative order. Bearing a rider puts no restrictions on the actions the mount can take, and it moves and acts as it wishes. It might flee from combat, rush to attack and devour a badly injured foe, or otherwise act against your wishes.

In either case, if the mount provokes an opportunity attack while you're on it, the attacker can target you or the mount.

rule:underwater-combat.description:
When adventurers pursue sahuagin back to their undersea homes, fight off sharks in an ancient shipwreck, or find themselves in a flooded dungeon room, they must fight in a challenging environment. Underwater the following rules apply.

When making a melee weapon attack, a creature that doesn't have a swimming speed (either natural or granted by magic) has disadvantage on the attack roll unless the weapon is a dagger, javelin, shortsword, spear, or trident.

A ranged weapon attack automatically misses a target beyond the weapon's normal range. Even against a target within normal range, the attack roll has disadvantage unless the weapon is a crossbow, a net, or a weapon that is thrown like a javelin (including a spear, trident, or dart).

Creatures and objects that are fully immersed in water have resistance to fire damage.

rule:attunement.description:
Some magic items require a creature to form a bond with them before their magical properties can be used. This bond is called attunement, and certain items have a prerequisite for it. If the prerequisite is a class, a creature must be a member of that class to attune to the item. (If the class is a spellcasting class, a monster qualifies if it has spell slots and uses that class's spell list.) If the prerequisite is to be a spellcaster, a creature qualifies if it can cast at least one spell using its traits or features, not using a magic item or the like.

Without becoming attuned to an item that requires attunement, a creature gains only its nonmagical benefits, unless its description states otherwise. For example, a magic shield that requires attunement provides the benefits of a normal shield to a creature not attuned to it, but none of its magical properties.

Attuning to an item requires a creature to spend a short rest focused on only that item while being in physical contact with it (this can't be the same short rest used to learn the item's properties). This focus can take the form of weapon practice (for a weapon), meditation (for a wondrous item), or some other appropriate activity. If the short rest is interrupted, the attunement attempt fails. Otherwise, at the end of the short rest, the creature gains an intuitive understanding of how to activate any magical properties of the item, including any necessary command words.

An item can be attuned to only one creature at a time, and a creature can be attuned to no more than three magic items at a time. Any attempt to attune to a fourth item fails; the creature must end its attunement to an item first. Additionally, a creature can't attune to more than one copy of an item. For example, a creature can't attune to more than one ring of protection at a time.

A creature's attunement to an item ends if the creature no longer satisfies the prerequisites for attunement, if the item has been more than 100 feet away for at least 24 hours, if the creature dies, or if another creature attunes to the item. A creature can also voluntarily end attunement by spending another short rest focused on the item, unless the item is cursed.

rule:ritual.description:
Certain spells have a special tag: ritual. Such a spell can be cast following the normal rules for spellcasting, or the spell can be cast as a ritual. The ritual version of a spell takes 10 minutes longer to cast than normal. It also doesn't expend a spell slot, which means the ritual version of a spell can't be cast at a higher level.

To cast a spell as a ritual, a spellcaster must have a feature that grants the ability to do so. The cleric and the druid, for example, have such a feature. The caster must also have the spell prepared or on his or her list of spells known, unless the character's ritual feature specifies otherwise, as the wizard's does.

rule:food-and-water.description:
Characters who don't eat or drink suffer the effects of exhaustion. Exhaustion caused by lack of food or water can't be removed until the character eats and drinks the full required amount.

A character needs one pound of food per day and can make food last longer by subsisting on half rations. Eating half a pound of food in a day counts as half a day without food.

A character can go without food for a number of days equal to 3 + his or her Constitution modifier (minimum 1). At the end of each day beyond that limit, a character automatically suffers one level of exhaustion.

A normal day of eating resets the count of days without food to zero.

A character needs one gallon of water per day, or two gallons per day if the weather is hot. A character who drinks only half that much water must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or suffer one level of exhaustion at the end of the day. A character with access to even less water automatically suffers one level of exhaustion at the end of the day.

If the character already has one or more levels of exhaustion, the character takes two levels in either case.

rule:flanking.description: When a creature and at least one ally are on directly opposite sides of an enemy and both are within reach of it, each of them has advantage on melee attack rolls against that enemy. Ranged attackers get no benefit, and a creature that can't see its target can't flank. It speeds fights up, but it makes outnumbering decisive, so turn it on knowing it rewards the side with more bodies.

rule:hitting-cover.description: When a ranged attack misses a target that is behind cover, the DM can rule that the shot strikes the cover instead if the roll would have hit the cover's own AC. Handy for destructible barriers, an ally being used as a shield, or a hostage held in front of a foe.

rule:cleaving-through-creatures.description: When a melee attack reduces an undamaged creature to 0 hit points and damage is left over, that extra damage carries to another creature within reach and range, as though the attack also struck it. No new roll is made. It lets a single heavy blow drop more than one minion.

rule:lingering-injuries.description: When a creature takes a critical hit, drops to 0 hit points without dying outright, or fails a death saving throw by 5 or more, the DM can roll on an injuries table for a lasting wound: a lost eye, a broken limb, internal damage, a scar that hampers checks. It adds grit and consequence; pair it with a way for the injury to heal over time.

rule:massive-damage.description: When a creature takes damage from a single source equal to or greater than half its hit point maximum, it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or suffer a system shock: stunned until the end of its next turn, knocked prone, or left unable to take reactions. It makes one huge hit genuinely frightening.

rule:morale.description: Rather than fighting to the last hit point, creatures may break and flee or surrender when a battle turns against them. The DM can call for a check (often a Wisdom save or a simple flat roll) when a side loses its leader, drops below half its number, or takes a sudden heavy loss. It keeps fights from grinding on after the outcome is decided.

rule:disarm.description: A creature can use one of its attacks to try to knock an object out of a target's grasp. The attacker makes an attack roll contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. The defender has advantage if it is larger or holds the item in two or more hands, and disadvantage if it is smaller. On a success, the target drops the item.

rule:overrun.description: When a creature wants to move through a hostile creature's space, it can try to force its way through. As part of its move it makes a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics); the larger of the two has advantage. On a success it can move through the space once this turn.

rule:tumble.description: A creature can try to dive, roll, or slip through a hostile creature's space. Using part of its movement, it makes a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by the target's Dexterity (Acrobatics). On a success it can move through the space once this turn, though that space still counts as difficult terrain.

rule:shove-aside.description: A variant of the shove: instead of pushing a target straight back or knocking it prone, the attacker can shove it 5 feet to one side. Because sidestepping a braced creature is harder, the defender has advantage on the contest. Useful for clearing a doorway or a path past a guard.

rule:mark.description: As a variant, a creature can mark a target it hits with a melee attack. Until the end of the marker's next turn, if the marked target moves out of the marker's reach or attacks anyone else, the marker can make one special melee attack against it as a reaction. It gives frontline martials a way to hold a line and protect allies.

rule:climb-onto-a-bigger-creature.description: A creature at least one size smaller than a foe can try to climb onto it. It moves into the target's space and makes a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by the target's Dexterity (Acrobatics). On a success it clings on, moving with the creature and gaining advantage on attacks against it; the target can use an action to try to shake it off.

rule:gritty-realism.description: A rest variant: a short rest is 8 hours and a long rest is 7 days. Recovery slows to a crawl, so a single adventuring day can stretch across a week or more and hit points and spell slots become precious. It suits grounded, survival-flavored campaigns and stretches the in-world calendar.

rule:epic-heroism.description: A rest variant: a short rest is 5 minutes and a long rest is 1 hour. Resources refresh quickly, so a group can face many encounters in a day and lean on its big abilities often. It suits pulpy, high-action games and pushes the challenge toward encounter design rather than attrition.

rule:slow-natural-healing.description: Creatures do not regain lost hit points at the end of a long rest. Instead, at the end of a long rest a creature may spend Hit Dice to heal, the same way it does on a short rest. It keeps wounds meaningful and makes healing magic and downtime matter, without stopping recovery entirely.

rule:encumbrance.description: A variant that tracks weight more strictly. Carrying more than your Strength score times 5 pounds leaves you encumbered: your speed drops by 10 feet. Carrying more than your Strength times 10 pounds leaves you heavily encumbered: your speed drops by 20 feet and you have disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws that use Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution. It gives loot and heavy gear real weight.

reference:difficulty-classes.blurb: Set a check's DC by how hard the task is.
reference:difficulty-classes.note: When in doubt, call it Medium (15). For a group check, the task succeeds if at least half the group succeeds.

reference:travel-pace.blurb: How far a party covers on foot, and the trade-off for hurrying or creeping.
reference:travel-pace.note: Difficult terrain halves the pace. Marching more than 8 hours in a day risks exhaustion: a Constitution save each extra hour, DC 10 + 1 per hour past 8.

reference:skills-by-ability.blurb: Which ability score each skill is tied to.
rows: Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Perception, Survival
reference:skills-by-ability.note: A passive score is 10 plus every modifier that would apply to the check, with no roll. Passive Perception is the one you will reach for most.

reference:light-sources.blurb: Each source sheds bright light, then dim light beyond it. In dim light, Perception checks that rely on sight are made with disadvantage; in darkness a creature without darkvision is effectively blinded.
reference:light-sources.note: A hooded lantern can be lowered to shed only dim light in a 5-ft radius. Darkvision lets a creature treat dim light as bright and darkness as dim (in shades of gray) out to its range.

reference:exhaustion-track.blurb: Levels of exhaustion stack, and each level includes the effects of the levels below it. Finishing a long rest, with food and drink, removes one level.
rows: Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws

reference:actions-in-combat.blurb: On your turn you move up to your speed and take one action, plus one bonus action if a feature grants one and one free interaction with an object. You also get one reaction each round, which can be used on another creature's turn.
rows: One melee or ranged attack (more if you have Extra Attack)
Gain extra movement equal to your speed
Your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks this turn
Attacks against you have disadvantage; you make Dex saves with advantage
Give an ally advantage on one check, or on their next attack against a foe next to you
Make a Stealth check to become unseen
Prepare an action to trigger on a condition you name (spends your reaction)
Make a Perception or Investigation check to find something
Cast a spell with a casting time of one action
Interact with a second object, or use one that needs an action
reference:actions-in-combat.note: The 2024 rules add the Influence, Study, Utilize, and Magic actions and fold some of the above into them, but the economy (one action, one bonus action, one reaction, your move, one free object interaction) is unchanged.

reference:object-armor-class-and-hit-poi.blurb: Improvised AC and HP for smashing or destroying objects.
reference:object-armor-class-and-hit-poi.note: HP by size (a resilient object doubles these): Tiny 2d6 (7), Small 3d6 (10), Medium 4d6 (14), Large 5d6 (18). Objects are immune to poison and psychic damage. Big objects (a wall, the ground) are effectively indestructible in a single turn; give them a section with its own HP instead.

reference:improvising-damage.blurb: Rough damage for hazards and effects you invent on the spot, scaled to land about right for the party.
reference:improvising-damage.note: Setback is a nuisance (a caltrop, a shove into a brazier), dangerous is a real threat (a falling chandelier), deadly can drop a character (a plume of lava). Single-source anchors: a torch 1d4 fire, a small fire 1d10, exposure to lava 10d10.

reference:environmental-hazards.blurb: Quick calls for the common survival threats.
rows: 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 ft fallen, to a max of 20d6; you land prone unless you avoid the damage
You can hold your breath for 1 + your Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds)
Once out of breath you last a number of rounds equal to your Con modifier (minimum 1), then drop to 0 HP and are dying
DC 10 Constitution save each hour or gain 1 level of exhaustion; cold resistance or immunity auto-succeeds
DC 5 Con save each hour, rising by 1 per hour, or gain 1 level of exhaustion; disadvantage in medium or heavy armor or without water
You can swim in it for a number of minutes equal to your Con score before a DC 10 Con save each minute or gain 1 level of exhaustion
reference:environmental-hazards.note: Suffocation ignores temporary hit points. A creature dropped to 0 by suffocation is unconscious and dying as usual.

reference:monster-statistics-by-challeng.blurb: Ballpark numbers to invent or reskin a creature on the fly and keep it about the right power for its CR.
reference:monster-statistics-by-challeng.note: Ranges are guidance, not hard rules: set AC, attack, and save DC near the CR row, pick HP within the band, and aim total damage per round at the damage column. CR 21-30 continues upward in the DMG (AC to about 23, attack to +14, save DC to 24).

reference:magic-item-rarity.blurb: Rarity roughly tracks the tier of play an item suits, and sets a ballpark value.
